ev.q: From 2021 to 2022, global coverage with the first dose of diphtheria-tetanus-pertussis–containing vaccine increased from 86% to 89%
the DTPcv1-to-DTPcv3 dropout rate (the percentage of children who received DTPcv1 but did not receive DTPcv3) was higher among low-income countries
WHO and UNICEF estimates of global DTPcv1 coverage increased from 86% in 2021 to 89% in 2022, but remained below 2019 coverage (90%)
the number of zero-dose children (14.3 million) decreased 21%, from 18.1 million in 2021
was higher among low-income countries (12%) than among lower-middle–income (5%), upper-middle–income (3%), or high-income (3%) countries
Among the 194 WHO countries, 73 (38%) experienced at least a 5% decline in DTPcv3 coverage from 2019 to 2021
documents progress toward improving coverage with respect to the IA2030 strategy
This report reviews trends in World Health Organization and UNICEF immunization coverage estimates at global, regional, and national levels through 2022
Estimated vaccination coverage, by World Health Organization Region, vaccine, and dose in series — worldwide, 2022

methods_quotes.q: DTPcv1-to-DTPcv3 and DTPcv1-to-MCV1 dropout rates were calculated as the percentage of children who received DTPcv1 but not DTPcv3 or MCV1, respectively.
WHO and UNICEF produce Estimates of National Immunization Coverage (WUENIC) at the national, regional, and global level based on review of country-specific data
Trends in vaccine coverage are also examined by World Bank economic classification.
